summary: Replace ShipRight's hand-built sign-in (own JWT, refresh tokens, password reset, Company/User tables, IsAdmin flag) with ASP.NET Core Identity backed by the existing Dapper-style data access (no EF Core), add the roles Admin, Operator and Viewer, add Google sign-in, and scope users, logins and roles per company (CompanyId). Decided: existing accounts and passwords keep working; desktop/local mode needs no sign-in and switches over transparently with no loss of data or projects; anyone can sign in with Google and a new company is created for them as Admin; no teammates for now, so every company has exactly one person (its Admin) and no invite or user-management screen is built. Still open: what an Operator or Viewer would be allowed to do once the roles are enforced.

ask.text: Operator and Viewer exist as roles, but nobody can be given them yet. When they are used later, what should each be allowed to do in ShipRight? For example, can a Viewer see projects and builds but not start a deploy?
ask.why: It decides which actions the server must block for each role now (so the rules are ready and tested), and which buttons the screens hide or disable.

options.label: Admin does everything; Operator can build and deploy but not change settings or servers; Viewer is read-only
options.consequence: Three clear levels. Operators run builds, deploys and backups; only Admins change project, server, secret and account settings; Viewers can look but not act.

options.label: Admin does everything; Operator and Viewer both read-only for now
options.consequence: Simplest to test, but Operator and Viewer would be identical until a later change.

options.label: Admin and Operator do everything; Viewer is read-only
options.consequence: Only one restriction to enforce: Viewers cannot change anything.

coverage.note: Roles Admin, Operator, Viewer; desktop mode needs no auth; Google first sign-in creates a new company with that person as Admin; no teammates for now.
Existing users, companies and password hashes stay valid; no invite data needed.
What Operator and Viewer may do is still to confirm; records stay scoped by CompanyId.
Password and email rules to assume once permissions are settled.
Google button and error states to assume.
Email stays globally unique; double sign-up must not create two companies.
No teammates, so no user lists to page or search.
No removal of users or accounts is part of this change.
Email and Google profile name stored; passwords never logged.
Lockout and session lifetime defaults to assume.
